claim: In 2026 the road to the Lagos de Covadonga is closed to private traffic during Easter (Mar 28-Apr 12 with some bridges), May weekends, the full Jun 1-Oct 18 stretch, plus Oct 24-25/31 and Nov 1-2; during regulated days only authorised vehicles (reduced mobility, refuge guests) may drive up.
quote: the access road to the Lakes will remain closed to traffic from 00:00 to 24:00 ... Only authorized vehicles—those with reduced mobility documentation or refuge reservations—can access the road.

claim: The PR-PNPE 2 lakes loop is a low-difficulty 5 km / 2.5 h long route (or 3 km / 1 h short version) starting at the Buferrera car park with only ~50 m of elevation, passing the Príncipe and Entrelagos viewpoints, the Buferrera mines, Lake Ercina and Lake Enol.
quote: Long route: 5 km, 2.5 hours ... Short route: 3 km, 1 hour ... Altitude gain/loss: 50 meters ... Difficulty level: Low

claim: The Covadonga lakes circular route is around 6 km of low difficulty and one of the most accessible in the park, taking in glacial lakes, beech forests, viewpoints and remains of mining activity.
quote: circular route about six kilometres long and of low difficulty that allows you to enjoy glacial lakes, beech forests, spectacular viewpoints and remains of mining activity

claim: The Sanctuary of Covadonga (basilica and Santa Cueva) is open 365 days a year and entry is free, though visitors are asked to respect mass times.
quote: abren todos los días del año de 8 h a 20 h ... se ruega a los visitantes que respeten los horarios de misas y cultos

claim: Entry to the basilica itself is free; a typical schedule is 09:00-13:30 and 15:30-19:00 (extending in peak season), and during busy periods sanctuary parking is regulated with shuttle service replacing direct car access.
quote: La entrada al templo en sí suele ser gratuita como lugar de culto ... 09:00–13:30 y 15:30–19:00 ... se limita el acceso con regulación de tráfico y aparcamiento vigilado

claim: The Bulnes funicular costs €17.61 one-way / €22.16 round-trip for adults and €4.32/€6.71 for children 4-12 in 2026, running every 30 minutes (high season ~10:00-20:00, low season ~10:00-18:00) and covering 2,227 m with a 400 m climb in about 7 minutes.
quote: Adult one-way: €17.61 ... Adult round-trip: €22.16 ... Children (4-12) one-way: €4.32 ... around 7 minutes to traverse 2,227 meters with a 400-meter elevation change

claim: Bulnes splits into Bulnes de Abajo and Bulnes de Arriba (El Castillo) 600 m higher, with the upper village giving the best Texu canal views and the surroundings offering panoramas of the Naranjo de Bulnes (Picu Urriellu, 2,519 m).
quote: Bulnes de Abajo (lower village) and Bulnes de Arriba/El Castillo (upper village) ... 600 meters higher and offers the best views of the Texu Canal

claim: Arriondas to the Lagos de Covadonga is about 29 km by road, roughly 45 minutes' drive — inside the 30 km radius from Casa Marcial, with Covadonga sanctuary at roughly 17 km along the same route.
quote: La distancia entre Arriondas y Lagos de Covadonga es 29 km

claim: Poncebos (base of the Bulnes funicular and Cares gorge trailhead) is about 44 km / 48 minutes from Arriondas — outside the 30 km radius but commonly combined as a longer half-day from the area.
quote: Arriondas to Poncebos by car: The distance is 44 kilometers and the driving time is approximately 48 minutes

claim: Aipol Aventura charges €35 adult / €25 child (under 12) for the 2026 Sella descent; price includes modern 1-3 seat canoes, paddles, life vests, waterproof container, parking, hot showers, and return transport; minimum age 5, minimum height 1.15 m, must know how to swim
quote: Adultos: €35 per person; Children (under 12): €25 per person; Pets: Free; Optional picnic: €5 (Asturian) or €7 (vegetarian/gluten-free)... canoas modernas de 1, 2 y 3 plazas, remos, bidón estanco y chalecos... Minimum age: 5 years old; Minimum height: 1.15 meters

claim: Frontera Verde offers two Sella routes: Arriondas-Toraño (8 km, 1.5-2 h) and Arriondas-Omedina (14 km, 3.5-4 h); €35 adult / €25 child, €45 on International Descent day (Aug 8 2026); picnic +€5; return van to Arriondas continuous from 14:00, river closes 18:00
quote: Adults: €35/person; Children (5-12 years): €25/child... International descent (Aug 8): €45/person... Arriondas to Toraño: 8 km, approximately 1.5-2 hours; Arriondas to Omedina: 14 km, approximately 3.5-4 hours... Recogidas a partir de las 14:00 ininterrumpidamente

claim: TurAventura prices scale by group size: €25/person for 1-10, down to €17-18 for 40+, €15 for children under 12; International Descent priced at €30/person
quote: 1-10 people: €25/person; 11-20 people: €22/person; 21-40 people: €19-20/person; 40+ people: €17-18/person; Children under 12: €15/person. International Descent: €30/person

claim: The 88th Descenso Internacional del Sella race is Saturday 8 August 2026, departing from Arriondas bridge at 12:00; declared a Fiesta de Interés Turístico Internacional with cannon-fire start, 'Asturias, patria querida' anthem, the Tren Fluvial spectator train, and traditional fabada + arroz con leche meal at Campos de la Oba (Lloviu)
quote: Date: Saturday, August 8, 2026. Start Time: 12:00 h (noon) from Arriondas facilities... A solemn rendition of 'Asturias, patria querida'... Cannon fire marking the official start... The 'Tren Fluvial' (river train)... Conclusion at Campos de la Oba (Lloviu) with traditional Asturian meal featuring fava beans and rice pudding

claim: Race-day timetable: 8:00-11:30 kayak assembly, 11:00 folk parade with traditional bands, 12:00 cannon start, first paddlers reach Ribadesella 13:10-13:45, prize ceremony 17:00 at Ribadesella bridge, then evening cider and concerts; race covers 20 km Arriondas to Ribadesella
quote: 8:00-11:30: Kayak assembly and boat inspections; 11:00: Folk parade with traditional bands; 12:00: Cannon shot and official departure from Arriondas bridge; 13:10-13:45: First paddlers arrive in Ribadesella; 17:00: Prize ceremony at Ribadesella bridge

claim: Rafting takes place on the upper Sella between Campurriondi and Estayos (Class II with a Class III finish at Los Estayos), in 6-8-person rafts with certified guide; season March 1 to October 31, best flow March-May from Picos snowmelt
quote: Class II level, with wide passages and predictable rapids suitable for beginners, though the final section 'Los Estayos' is classified as Class III... between Campurriondi and Estayos (where the Dobra River meets the Sella). The season runs from March 1 to October 31

claim: Canyoning trips depart Arriondas across canyons including Cuevón de Pruneda, Carangas, La Molina (Cabrales), Vallegón, Vivoli, Tinganón (Ribadesella) and family-friendly Rubo; prices €50-€80 for 2 to 4¾-hour sessions
quote: Cuevón de Pruneda (medium-high level); Barranco Carangas (multiple difficulty levels); Barranco La Molina in Cabrales; Barranco Vallegón (medium level); Barranco Vivoli (medium-high level); La Cueva'l Tinganón in Ribadesella; Barranco Rubo (family-friendly option)... Prices range from €50–€80

claim: Horseback rides leave Arriondas/Cangas de Onís in 1- or 2-hour formats at €25 adult / €20 child (≤12), passing the village of Coviella with hórreos and an 18th-c. palace before mountain views of the Sueve and Picos; helmet, rain cape, guide and insurance included; minimum rider height 1.30 m
quote: 1-hour rides (most common for beginners); 2-hour rides. Pricing: €25 per adult; €20 per child (up to 12 years old)... Minimum height of 1.30 meters... passing through the village of Coviella where you can see traditional Asturian constructions (hórreos) and an 18th-century palace

claim: Ulex Paragliding Club School is the Arriondas-based paragliding operator at Finca Fundición de Coviella-El portazgo (tel +34 985 841 282), federated with the Principality of Asturias and offering tandem flights with instructor for first-time flyers
quote: Ulex Paragliding Club School is located at Finca Fundición de Coviella-El portazgo, 33540 Arriondas, with contact number +985 841 282... two-seater paragliders and qualified pilot instructors who make flights with those interested in trying flying without needing to take a learning course

claim: Rana Sella rents high-end e-MTBs from the Coviella (Arriondas) base, using carbon-frame MMR bikes with internal batteries and Bosch 4th-gen motors
quote: Bicycles are available at facilities in Finca La Fundición de Coviella, in Arriondas. They offer high-end electric bicycles from the Asturian firm MMR, with carbon frames, internal batteries, and Bosch fourth-generation motor systems

claim: Senda del Oso bike-rental centre charges €40/bike/day for Conor 29"/27.5" e-bikes with a €180 card hold; in early 2026 the operator is switching from rear-motor to centre-motor models to open routes beyond the gentle green ones
quote: Rental prices are €40 per bike per day, with a €180 credit card deposit that is refunded upon return in perfect condition... they are making changes for 2026, moving away from rear motor e-bikes to allow usage beyond just green routes and low-incline paths

claim: Tito Bustillo cave is open 4 March to 30 October 2026, Wednesday to Sunday, first tour 10:15 and last tour 17:00, closed Mondays/Tuesdays and 8-9 August, with 15 visitors per slot and 150/day cap.
quote: Open from 4th March to 30th October 2026. Wednesdays to Sundays, from 10:15 h. (first tour) to 17:00 h. (last tour). Closed Mondays, Tuesdays, 8-9 August. Maximum 15 participants per slot, 150 per day.

claim: Tito Bustillo general admission is 4.14 EUR (reduced 2.12 EUR) with free entry on Wednesdays; tickets for visits from 1 July 2026 go on sale 1 April 2026.
quote: General admission is €4.14, and reduced admission is €2.12. Entrance is free on Wednesdays. Tickets to visit the cave from July 1 will go on sale on April 1, 2026.

claim: Guided tours inside Tito Bustillo cave are conducted only in Spanish; English audio guides and a QR-code English tour are provided as alternatives, and the on-site Cave Art Centre museum has bilingual Spanish/English displays.
quote: Guided visits are only in Spanish ... visitors are offered two audios in English ... a QR code outside before the bridge ... links to a tour in English ... modern museum with lots of audiovisual and interactive displays and with information in both Spanish and English.

claim: Visitors must arrive at the Centro de Arte Rupestre reception desk at least 30 minutes before their cave time slot or they lose entry; the centre sits about 300 m from the cave entrance and serves as the orientation museum and backup if cave tickets are sold out.
quote: Visitors must arrive at the reception desk at least 30 minutes before their scheduled visit time to confirm entry, as failure to do so means losing the right to enter the cave.

claim: The 'Roman' bridge of Cangas de Onís is in fact a 14th-century medieval bridge built under Alfonso XI of Castile spanning the Sella; a replica of the Victory Cross was hung from its central arch in 1939 after the Virgin of Covadonga returned from Paris.
quote: built in the times of King Alfonso XI of Castile in the 14th century ... One of the most iconic elements of the bridge is the large Victoria Cross that hangs from its central arch ... installed in 1939 when the Virgin of Covadonga returned from Paris.

claim: The Iglesia de la Santa Cruz in Cangas de Onís is an 8th-century pre-Romanesque royal foundation, consecrated 27 October 737 by king Favila, that once held Pelayo's Cruz de la Victoria and was rebuilt in 1632 and again in 1950 after Civil War destruction.
quote: here were consecrated altars to Christ by the priest Asterion on the day 300 of the year ... era 775, corresponding to October 27, 737 ... many modifications (in 1632 and in 1950 after destruction during the Spanish Civil War).

claim: The Santa Cruz crypt encloses a Neolithic/Bronze-age dolmen with engraved orthostats; visits are run via the Cangas de Onís tourist office, cost 2 EUR, last about 10-15 minutes, are closed Mondays and Tuesdays with last entry at 13:00, and guided slots run during Easter and summer.
quote: closed on Mondays and Tuesdays ... last entry is at 1:00 PM ... cost of entry is two euros ... Guided visits are available during Easter week and summer ... reservation at the Tourist Office of Cangas de Onís is necessary.

claim: The Covadonga sanctuary complex 10 km from Cangas de Onís bundles the pink neo-Romanesque Basilica (1877-1901), the Santa Cueva chapel above a waterfall housing the tombs of Pelayo and other Asturian royalty, the Pelayo monument, and a small museum; visits are free and open daily roughly 08:30-21:30 outside Mass.
quote: comprises the Holy Cave, Basilica, Covadonga Museum, San Fernando Collegiate Church, and Monument to King Pelayo ... You can visit it daily from 8:30 to 21:30, except on worshiping hours ... no entrance fee to enter the Holy Cave or the Basilica.

claim: Tito Bustillo is part of the UNESCO 'Cave Art of Northern Spain' inscription and tickets sell out fast in high season; Mondays and Tuesdays are closed and booking weeks ahead online is strongly advised.
quote: Cueva de Tito Bustillo ... UNESCO-listed Palaeolithic cave art ... book well in advance ... closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

claim: Playa de Gulpiyuri is a ~40-metre-long inland beach with white sand fed by the Bay of Biscay through cliff channels; designated a Natural Monument and pedestrian-only with vehicles prohibited.
quote: about forty metres long... the Bay of Biscay is just a few metres away and only flows under the cliffs

claim: Reviewers warn of €100-€200 parking fines for unmarked restricted zones at Gulpiyuri and recommend visiting at high tide; low tide leaves it 'a tiny puddle'.
quote: received €100-€200 fines for parking in unmarked restricted zones... At low tide, it appears as 'a tiny puddle'

claim: Gulpiyuri requires a 400 m walk from a parking area off the A8 at the eastern end of Naves; access from San Antolín beach or Naves village is pedestrian only.
quote: Gulpiyuri is a 400m walk from a parking area just off the A8 at the eastern end of Naves

claim: Playa de Santa Marina in Ribadesella is a ~1 km urban beach with full promenade, lifeguards, amphibious chair, showers, toilets, car/bike parking and chiringuitos; holds the Q for Tourist Quality certification since 2004.
quote: Smoke-free beach | Rescue service | Amphibious chair | Showers | Toilets | Car and bicycle parking | Chiringuitos

claim: Dinosaur footprints are visible at the western end of Santa Marina beach near the Pozu watchpoint in Ribadesella, marked on the vertical cliff face.
quote: the most spectacular and easy to see are the ones near Santa Marina Beach, where the watchpoint Pozu is located

claim: Ribadesella has an 'old town vibe and beach vibe', with a colonial seafront promenade, historic centre, viewpoints and varied restaurants; cider bars and seafood eateries cluster behind the fishing harbour.
quote: Ribadesella with its old town vibe and beach vibe was one of favorite places on the coast of Asturias

claim: Cuevas del Mar is a 125 m triangular cove at the Cuevas River mouth near Nueva (Llanes), famed for karst sea-arches, caves and tunnels carved into limestone; shallow protected water makes it family-friendly.
quote: karst rock formations sculpted by the sea: arches, cracks and cavities that turn the environment into a true geological spectacle

claim: Cuevas del Mar has a large car park, rescue service (Jun 14–Sep 8), showers, toilets and catering; moderate waves and considered safe for swimming; pets prohibited Jun 1–Sep 30.
quote: Rescue service | Showers | Toilets | Parking | Catering service

claim: Playa de Vega is a ~2 km surf beach with rare preserved dune system, Jurassic clay cliffs and unique European fluorite deposits; powerful waves create dangerous swimming conditions but ideal surf with breaks like 'Superman' on the east end.
quote: ideal for surfing, with consistent swells and breaks like 'Superman' peak at the eastern section

claim: Vega works on all tides with right and left peaks along the full 1.5 km of beach; northwest-facing pickup and rarely crowded even when waves are firing.
quote: right and left peaks along the entire beach that work well with all tides... Even when there are waves, it's not likely to be crowded

claim: Playa de San Antolín is a 1200 m beach next to the Romanesque church of San Antolín de Bedón with large car park, viewpoint and surf services; highly dangerous for bathing due to strong waves but popular with surfers.
quote: highly dangerous for bathing due to its exposure to strong waves, but it is very popular with surfers

claim: San Antolín is a sheltered beach break working year-round, best on northwest groundswells with offshore south winds and around low-to-rising tide; eastern part holds tubing rights.
quote: Best around low tide when the tide is rising... The eastern part usually has the best waves, with quite tubing rights

claim: Arriondas to Ribadesella is roughly 19–21 km by road, about 19–22 minutes' drive.
quote: driving distance between Arriondas and Ribadesella is 21 km, and the drive would take approximately 19 minutes

claim: Arriondas to Playa de Gulpiyuri is about 19.5 miles (~31 km) by road, roughly 28 minutes' drive — borderline at the 30 km limit.
quote: The fastest way to get from Playa de Gulpiyuri to Arriondas is by car, which takes 28 minutes. The distance between Playa de Gulpiyuri and Arriondas is 19 miles

claim: Mirador del Fitu sits at 597 m on the AS-260 between Arriondas and Colunga, ~11 km from each, with a 360º panorama spanning the Sueve, Ponga, Picos de Europa and the Cantabrian coast; the concrete watchtower was inaugurated in 1927.
quote: The viewpoint stands at 597 meters in the Sierra del Sueve, offering a spectacular 360º vision... Take the AS-260 road connecting Arriondas and Colunga. The viewpoint is equidistant from both towns at approximately 11 kilometers away.

claim: Fitu has a small car park at the mirador and a larger gravel overflow lot ~100 m further up near telecom antennas; access is free, 24/7, but the road can close in snow/ice.
quote: There's a small car park right at the mirador and a second, larger gravel parking area 100 meters further up (next to some telecom antennas).

claim: The PR-AS 71 from Fitu to Pico Pienzu summit is 11.73 km out-and-back, ~700 m of elevation gain (577 m to 1,145 m), classified Dura (hard), 3-5 hours, passing the Majada de Bustacu shieling; vultures, choughs, Asturcón horses and fallow deer are commonly seen.
quote: It is common to see vultures, choughs, Asturcón horses and fallow deer, the faunistic symbol of the Sierra del Sueve.

claim: The Sierra del Sueve is the last refuge of the Asturcón, an ancient muscular pony about four feet tall that the Romans used in mine work; its dark herds roam the high pastures freely.
quote: the asturcón, one of the world's oldest horses, a muscular and agile animal just four feet high, whose dark wild herds blend into a dark green landscape.

claim: The Plan Lagos shuttle buses do not stop at Mirador de la Reina; on regulated days you reach it only by taxi (which will halt on request, ~€10/adult round trip) or by bike — outside regulated periods or before the 8:30 am cutoff, drive up the CO-4 and park in the dedicated lot at the mirador.
quote: Unfortunately, the buses do not stop at the Mirador on their way to the Lakes.

claim: Mirador de la Reina sits at 910 m altitude roughly 8 km up the CO-4 from the Basilica of Covadonga, giving a wide circular panorama over the northern Picos de Europa, the Güeña valley meadows and, on clear days, the Bay of Biscay.
quote: Mirador de la Reina... 910 metros de altitud... amplio panorama circular de los Picos de Europa y vistas... Onís, Cangas de Onís y Covadonga.

claim: The Pico Pienzu summit (1,159 m, highest in the Sueve) returns coast-to-mountain views from the Picos to the Bay of Biscay with Gijón, Ribadesella, Colunga and Villaviciosa visible below; the trail starts directly at Fitu's car park.
quote: Picu Pienzu standing as the highest peak in the Sierra del Sueve at 1,159 meters... panoramic vistas range from the Picos de Europa mountains to the Bay of Biscay

claim: The CO-4 climb up to Mirador de la Reina includes sustained 12-14% grades, with the steepest precipice-edged stretch continuing beyond the mirador toward the Lakes — relevant for nervous drivers and cyclists.
quote: At the Mirador de la Reina there are slopes of 13% and 14%

claim: The Cueva-Exposición del Queso Cabrales in Arenas de Cabrales runs ~45-minute guided tours (two 20-min segments), with adult tickets €6, child €4, groups (15+) €4.50, max 20 people per tour, reservations by phone 985 84 67 02; cave is 10–15°C so bring layers.
quote: Approximately 45 minutes ... Adults: €6.00 Children: €4.00 Groups (15+ people): €4.50 per person ... Maximum capacity: 20 people per tour ... Cave temperature: 10-15°C

claim: Arriondas to Arenas de Cabrales is about 37–38 km by road (~40 min), placing the Cueva-Exposición just outside the 30 km radius but still an easy half-day from Casa Marcial.
quote: 37 Km - Distancia entre Arenas de Cabrales y Arriondas

claim: The Museo de la Sidra in Nava (Plaza Príncipe de Asturias) charges €4 adult / €3 child 6–16 / €2 child 3–5, with free admission on Tuesdays; winter hours Tue–Fri 11:00–14:00 & 16:00–19:00, Sat 11:00–15:00 & 16:30–20:00, Sun 11:00–14:00.
quote: Adults: €4. ... Children ages 6-16: €3. ... Tuesdays are free (no reservations needed). ... Tuesday to Friday: 11:00-14:00 and 16:00-19:00. Saturday: 11:00-15:00 and 16:30-20:00.

claim: Arriondas to Nava is about 34 km by road, just outside the strict 30 km radius but still a comfortable day-trip for the Museo de la Sidra and town sidrerías.
quote: 34 Km - Distancia entre NAVA y arriondas asturias

claim: Escanciado is the signature Asturian pour: cider is poured from height so the stream hits the rim of the glass, releasing CO2 and aromas; served at 12–14°C in a fine-crystal cider glass (12 cm tall, 9 cm opening), and the resulting 'culín' is drunk in one go before the foam dies.
quote: Escanciar consiste en verter la sidra natural tradicional asturiana desde una cierta altura, desde la botella al vaso, logrando que el chorro impacte en el borde del vaso

claim: Sidraturismo Asturias' official booking platform lists llagar visits including Castañón (€3+ basic tour, €9+ Castañón Experience with cask sampling and snacks), Sidra Cortina (€10+), Llagar Herminio (€12–€30 including farm-to-table options), and Sidra Viuda de Angelón (€4.50).
quote: Llagar Castañón ... €3.00 ... V2. Castañón Experience €9.00+ ... Llagar Herminio €12.00-€30.00 ... Sidra Viuda de Angelón €4.50

claim: Llagar Castañón sits at Los Pisones 90, Quintueles (Villaviciosa concejo) — family tradition since 1938, modern facility from 2011, with three sidraturismo formats by reservation; technically outside the 30 km radius from Arriondas.
quote: Castañón es un llagar con tradición familiar desde 1938 ... Los Pisones 90, 33314 Quintueles, Villaviciosa

claim: Sidrería Prida in the centre of Nava is a traditional Asturian cider-house restaurant rated ~4.4/5, with menús around €20 featuring dishes like bacalao-and-shrimp scrambled eggs, hake, and braised kid goat alongside natural cider service.
quote: Sidrería Prida ... traditional Asturian cider house ... menus around €20 for high-quality dining

claim: Cangas de Onís hosts a Sunday market every week from roughly 09:30–13:30 around the Iglesia de Santa María, with artisan Cabrales, Gamoneu and Beyos cheeses, fabes (white beans), honey, cured meats, basketry and ceramics — a 200-year tradition and one of the most important markets in the Picos region.
quote: El mercado se celebra cada domingo ... cerca de la Iglesia Parroquial de Santa María ... quesos artesanos de Cabrales, Gamoneu y Beyos

claim: Nava's Festival de la Sidra Natural takes place the second weekend of July (10 July 2026) and the preceding week, culminating Sunday with the International Competition for Escanciadores — useful timing context for anyone visiting Asturias in early summer.
quote: Natural Cider Festival, Nava. 10/07/2026

claim: Official Asturian tourism guidance: cider is poured one culín at a time (about 100 ml), the drinker downs it immediately because aeration fades within seconds, and a small splash is traditionally tipped onto the floor to rinse the next person's rim of the glass.
quote: A guide to enjoying Asturian cider
